newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-NAPOLI GET TO ITALY CUP FINAL ON PENALTY SHOOT-OUT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-NAPOLI GET TO ITALY CUP FINAL ON PENALTY SHOOT-OUT.

text.p: A penalty shoot-out took Napoli through to the Italian Cup final on Wednesday on a day of double disappointment for favourites Internazionale.

The victory, 5-3 on penalties after the two-legged tie ended 2-2 on aggregate, brought an explosion of fireworks from fans in the San Paolo stadium and revived memories of the glory days of Diego Maradona, the last man to lead Napoli to Cup honours in 1987.

Their hero was yet again a Latin American in a number 10 shirt -- Brazilian Beto who struck a goal in the 77th minute to level the second leg at 1-1 and put Napoli back on the path to a June final against Vicenza.
Inter, held 1-1 in the first leg in Milan, went into the match after learning their English coach Roy Hodgson would be leaving at the end of the season to manage premier league club Blackburn Rovers.

They went ahead in the 11th minute through Argentine midfielder Javier Zanetti, who spotted a gap in a line of seven Napoli players and blasted a shot past keeper Giuseppe Tagliatela from outside the area.

Reduced to 10 men when striker Maurizio Ganz was sent off in the 34th minute for a foul on Francesco Colonnese, Inter had looked like resisting a Napoli onslaught diminished by poor finishing until Beto saw his chance.
He broke through and found himself alone in front of goal to nudge the ball just wide of Gianluca Pagliuca.

With the aggregate score at 2-2 after extra time and 210 minutes of soccer, the semifinal was decided when nerves got the better of Inter defender Massimo Paganin, who served up a weak penalty straight into Tagliatela's grateful hands.
Napoli meet Vicenza in the final over two legs on June 4 and 11. The northern side, victors against Bologna in their semifinal, will be playing in their first Cup final in their 95-year history.

Inter had been favourites for the domestic cup among the last four. Although they are still in the UEFA Cup, their league title aspirations have taken a jolt. They lie third in serie A, seven points adrift of leaders Juventus.
